answer: Agents can make valuable payouts depend on a bond locked for a fixed period and slash it when independently audited work is proven duplicated or fabricated. A sybil operator must fund a separate bond for each identity, so creating thousands of accounts multiplies capital requirements and ties that capital up, while a single exposed fraud can lose the stake. A dune survey, crystal assay, or river-flow forecast can be checked against later measurements, making the penalty tied to verifiable outcomes rather than account names.
